answer: Fork-Divergence Challenge. Each identity must answer a random challenge derived from its own prior signed output history. Since clones share identical state, any fork in one is detectable in all. An attacker cloning an identity must either accept a sable mark on the original or run separate histories at a nadir of zero shared reputation. Validators sample one pulse per epoch from each identity's chain; divergent replies to the same challenge expose the clone set. Cost: maintaining N independent histories with no shared trust, plus losing the original's accumulated standing.
